headline: High-risk workflow pair: n8n’s default server-side execution and broad egress can amplify data leakage, capability conflicts, and cascading errors when paired with LlamaFactory.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between LlamaFactory and n8n, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, n8n can pass workflow content through files and nodes, and LlamaFactory is an LLM system that may ingest text as instructions if wired that way. The pathway requires unusual integration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n workflow nodes feed LlamaFactory-generated text back into an AI Agent node without provenance checks
IF a shared file or message channel is added between the two agents
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every handoff payload
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any workflow step that re-ingests model output as instructions
Review node inputs for prompt-like delimiters before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and can call many integrations, while LlamaFactory is a model system with no filesystem or network surfaces shown. If n8n routes sensitive workflow data into LlamaFactory prompts or logs, data can leave the original boundary in default workflows. The pair therefore has a plausible leakage path with sensitive multi-work-product blast radius.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process secrets, customer records, or other sensitive payloads
IF those payloads are forwarded into LlamaFactory prompts, training data, or logs
mitigations: Redact secrets before any LLM call
Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Separate sensitive workflows from AI workflows
Turn off verbose execution logging for sensitive jobs
Use a dedicated non-sensitive test workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write, shell execution, and broad egress; LlamaFactory is non-runnable and shows no write or shell capability. There is no direct same-resource write conflict proven, but if n8n orchestrates artifacts that LlamaFactory also consumes or emits, concurrent mutation of shared files or workflow state is plausible. Uncertainty about the exact shared resource pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same server directory or shared datastore
IF n8n Execute Command nodes mutate files that LlamaFactory also reads or writes via an external wrapper
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize access to any shared artifact
Avoid Execute Command on shared paths
Use immutable handoff files with versioned names

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools and downstream actions, so if it consumes LlamaFactory output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real-world workflow actions. LlamaFactory has no built-in verification surface shown, and n8n’s broad integrations make the blast radius potentially irreversible. This is a default-dangerous interaction unless explicit validation is added.
conditions: IF n8n uses LlamaFactory output to populate tool arguments or decision branches
IF no human or rule-based verification step is inserted before downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node
Require human approval for external side effects
Constrain AI output to structured schemas
Log and diff model outputs before execution
Disable auto-execution on untrusted model text

E_compliance.rationale: n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server, while LlamaFactory has no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated data flows from n8n into LlamaFactory prompts or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pairwise handoff, not either system alone.
conditions: IF the workflow processes EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data
IF LlamaFactory is used on that data without a documented retention and residency policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AI prompts
Document retention for every workflow node
Use separate environments for regulated workflows
Purge execution logs after review
Add a data-class gate before LLM calls
